KEY MESSAGE 1...Surge of warmth and humidity Wednesday ahead of
a cold front.

A frontal zone draped to our north will result in surface low 
pressure riding along it through Wednesday, pulling a cold front
across our area by late Wednesday. Ahead of this feature, 
southerly flow will boost the low-level warm air advection 
regime, resulting in much warmer air surging into our area. 
Wednesday's highs are forecast to mainly range in the low to mid
80s, with even some upper 80s to near 90 degrees possible over 
southern Delaware.

In addition, dew points will increase back through the 60s into
Wednesday. This will result in a much more humid feel over the 
next couple days, with it being the most humid on Wednesday 
(heat index values should approach 90F for areas from about 
Philadelphia south and east; away from the coast). There does 
not appear to be much in the way of forcing, therefore just a 
slight chance (less than 25%) for showers is expected. After the
front moves through, cooler air will briefly return on 
Thursday. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...A strong cold front passage on Friday will 
bring windy conditions, showers and potential for some 
thunderstorms, and colder temperatures into the weekend.

A sharp upper-level trough is forecast to arrive across the 
East Coast on Friday, then gradually lift out over the weekend. 
This will drive rapidly strengthening surface low pressure just 
north of our area Friday, with an associated strong cold front 
sweeping through. Guidance has come into consensus that the fast
moving cold frontal passage will occur between the mid 
afternoon to evening hours likely moving from our western most 
zones and offshore within about 3 hours or so.

A warm and increasingly moist airmass ahead of this system will
provide modest instability and decent boundary layer mixing as 
the strong cold front approaches on Friday. Large scale forcing 
for ascent will increase with the arrival of the robust upper- 
level trough and cold front, therefore showers will increase in 
coverage and intensity Thursday night into Friday. However, the 
exact details regarding the convective evolution remain unclear.
Some thunderstorms are possible given the strength of the 
system and instability, however this will ultimately depend on 
the magnitude of the instability and timing of the cold front. 
Cannot rule out some severe thunderstorm potential, especially 
if any more robust convection can materialize along the cold 
front.

While it will be mostly cloudy, strong warm advection will 
boost temperatures up well into the 70s and low 80s ahead of the
front. As surface pressure falls rapidly amid a strengthening 
southwesterly gradient, breezy conditions will likely develop 
outside of any showers and storms with gusts of 25-35 mph 
possible.

During and after cold frontal passage, strong cold air 
advection will occur as the sharp trough aloft sweeps through. 
This will support efficient mixing of winds aloft down toward 
the surface in the form of frequent wind gusts as temperatures 
plummet into the 50s then 40s overnight. Boundary layer winds 
could be as high as 40-50 mph for a few hours in the wake of the
front, which could warrant a Wind Advisory. The timing of the 
peak winds appears to be focused during the evening and 
overnight hours.

The coldest airmass so far this season will settle into the 
area Saturday into Saturday night. High temperatures Saturday 
are only in the low to mid 50s in most areas (40s north of 
I-78). Breezy conditions will continue, with northwest winds 
gusting 30-40 mph possible in the morning before gradually 
diminishing later in the day.


KEY MESSAGE 3...There is potential for widespread frost and 
freeze conditions Saturday night.

As strong surface high pressure settles nearly overhead into 
Saturday night, temperatures will cool significantly with 
radiational cooling. This should result in widespread low 
temperatures in the 30s Saturday night into Sunday morning, and 
potentially into the upper 20s north of I-78. This will 
introduce our first widespread frost and freeze potential of the
season. A freeze appears unlikely south of I-78, but the usual 
cold spots could drop to near the freezing mark. Otherwise, 
areas of frost are possible.

The airmass will start to modify Sunday and into early next 
week. Highs Sunday should rebound into the mid 50s to near 60 
degrees in most areas with winds 5-10 mph making for a much more
pleasant day compared to Saturday. There could be some frost 
potential Sunday night, but lows are likely to rebound into the 
upper 30s to low 40s in most areas. Temperatures will then 
rebound to near normal values, with highs well into the 60s 
early next week and dry weather expected.
